summary: The procurement claim is clear; one causal claim lacks support and the opening of section 1 circles before landing.

doc_points.title: Close does not return to the claim
doc_points.rationale: The reader finishes on the table and never hears why procurement matters more than policy.
doc_points.hint: End on the key claim from the first section.

comments.exact: Voluntary guidance has changed board behaviour across the ASX 200.
comments.prefix: the only document a vendor reads closely.
comments.title: Causal claim without support
comments.rationale: A director will ask what shows the guidance caused the change.
comments.hint: Support the sentence starting 'Voluntary guidance has changed…' or narrow it to what you can show.

comments.exact: Most Australian agencies now buy AI rather than build it.
comments.title: Unsourced claim
comments.hint: Add a source for the sentence starting 'Most Australian agencies now…'.

comments.exact: In an era of rapid technological change, organisations face new questions
comments.title: Scene-setting
comments.rationale: The reader waits for the point.
comments.hint: Rewrite as: Boards rarely change behaviour without enforcement and clear accountability for every outcome.

comments.exact: who owns the model's outputs once it is deployed?
comments.title: Question needs an answer
comments.rationale: The reader expects the author's view.
comments.hint: Consider: boards rarely act without enforcement.

comments.exact: Procurement teams always read the contract twice before award.
comments.title: Invented anchor

comments.exact: The contract is therefore where obligations are set, and it is often the only document a vendor reads closely.
comments.title: Strong point
comments.rationale: This is the most concrete claim in the opening.
comments.hint: Keep the sentence starting 'The contract is therefore where obligations are…' and move it first.
